subject: Art & Design
title: Crisis Branding: Rebuilding Trust After Scandal
description: One-minute skill: Crisis Branding: Rebuilding Trust After Scandal.

hook.text: In 1982, seven people died from cyanide-laced Tylenol. J&J's response became the gold standard of crisis branding.

buildup.text: A brand crisis can destroy decades of trust in hours. The response matters more than the crisis itself.

discovery.text: The crisis playbook: acknowledge immediately, take responsibility, act decisively, and communicate transparently.

twist.text: Some brands emerge stronger. Tylenol's share recovered because the recall proved J&J valued people over profit.

climax.text: BP spent $65 billion after its 2010 oil spill and rebranded with a green sunflower logo. Critics called it greenwashing.

punchline.text: Trust takes years to build and seconds to lose. Recovery is the real brand test.

quiz.question: Why is Tylenol's 1982 crisis response considered a gold standard?
options: They recalled all products immediately, prioritizing safety over profit
They blamed the retailer and avoided responsibility
They ignored the incident until media pressure forced action

details.summary: Crisis branding addresses how brands rebuild reputation after scandals, product failures, or public relations disasters. Johnson & Johnson's transparent response to the 1982 Tylenol poisoning became the gold standard.
details.whyItMatters: Every brand will face a crisis eventually. How it responds determines whether the crisis becomes a footnote or a permanent scar. Brands that accept responsibility quickly and act decisively tend to recover; those that deflect and delay often don't.
takeaways: J&J's Tylenol response became the gold standard for crisis handling
BP's defensive oil spill response deepened brand damage
Accepting responsibility quickly enables faster recovery

faq.question: What made J&J's Tylenol response so effective?
faq.answer: They immediately recalled 31 million bottles nationwide, cooperated fully with authorities, communicated transparently with the public, and introduced tamper-proof packaging.

faq.question: How long does brand recovery from a crisis typically take?
faq.answer: Minor crises can recover in weeks with swift response. Major scandals involving safety or deception can take years. Some brands never fully recover. The speed of recovery depends on prior brand equity, response authenticity, and whether the underlying problem is genuinely fixed.
